page: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare-metal server configuration within the Bare Metal SSD product family, engineered primarily for memory-intensive enterprise computing. Powered by a dedicated single-socket AMD EPYC 9354P processor running at 3.25 GHz, the instance delivers 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. It features 768 GB of high-frequency 5 GHz DDR5 memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 12 GB per virtual core. Local storage is provided by a 960 GB SSD, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server operates without dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Hardware benchmark testing highlights the impact of the Zen 4 x86_64 architecture and DDR5 subsystem. In synthetic compute evaluations, the system places in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core performance (3,179.99) and the top 25% for multi-core throughput (101,731.42), mirrored by a PassMark CPU score of 80,803.08 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 20,113. Memory subsystem evaluations demonstrate sustained uncached large-block throughput, delivering 351.41 GB/s in reads and 165.96 GB/s in writes, leading to a top-tier PassMark memory index of 3,143.69. Application tests show strong capabilities in in-memory workloads, handling 91.34 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining 48.07 GB/s of static web delivery.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this bare-metal profile stems from its dense DDR5 memory deployment paired with single-socket compute, eliminating virtualization hypervisor overhead. While CPU and memory throughput benchmark strongly across all standard tiers, the bundled 960 GB SSD represents a relatively modest capacity for a server with 768 GB of RAM, meaning secondary remote storage or external arrays may be necessary for large historical datasets. This hardware profile is best suited for large in-memory caching layers, enterprise in-memory databases, dense virtualization hosts, software compilation clusters, and mid-sized CPU-based LLM inference pipelines.
description: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare-metal server designed for memory-intensive workloads requiring dedicated x86_64 hardware. Built around an AMD EPYC 9354P processor clocked at 3.25 GHz, it supplies 32 physical cores and 64 threads alongside 768 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 system memory and a bundled 960 GB SSD. The platform contains no hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the top tier for single-core CPU execution and memory subsystem throughput, with uncached read speeds reaching 351.41 GB/s and write speeds hitting 165.96 GB/s. Application testing confirms robust performance in memory-bound services, achieving over 91 million Redis SET operations per second. A potential hardware tradeoff is the comparatively modest 960 GB local storage capacity relative to its 768 GB RAM footprint. The configuration is optimal for in-memory databases, large Redis caches, memory-bound data pipelines, and dense hypervisor virtualization.
